topic.title: Conditional utility of historical action information
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, do historical action codes improve click AUC beyond aligned item content and the supplied task masks in the strongest visible model?
topic.hypothesis: Historical action codes may supply predictive information beyond item fields and task-mask membership, but the compact evidence does not establish this. Inherit the strongest visible model and retain it unchanged as the utility control. Compare full historical-action use with action-blind and valid-history action-permutation treatments, preserving every event position, item field, history mask, task mask, auxiliary objective and the zero target action. Match representation capacity and training exposure, and measure prediction cost. Loss under permutation alone could reflect distribution disruption; concordant loss under retrained action-blind controls would support conditional action utility. Equal or better action-blind performance would falsify a useful incremental contribution in this setting. This does not identify total historical-feedback utility because task masks can retain feedback information. Reserve budget for control attribution and repetition; single-seed differences remain provisional.
